q: Equilibrium means a state of ____.
e: Equilibrium means a state of balance. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: There are two types of equilibrium; static equilibrium and ____ equilibrium.
e: There are two types of equilibrium; static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: Consider a book at rest on a table. The weight of a book gets balanced by the normal reaction force from the table to the book, resulting in ____ equilibrium.
e: Consider a book at rest on a table. The weight of a book gets balanced by the normal reaction force from the table to the book, resulting in static equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In a sealed bottle of soda, carbon dioxide is present in both the liquid phase and the ____ phase.
e: In a sealed bottle of soda, carbon dioxide is present in both the liquid phase and the gaseous phase. Gaseous is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Inside the sealed soda bottle, the two forms of carbon dioxide are in ____ equilibrium.
e: Inside the sealed soda bottle, the two forms of carbon dioxide are in dynamic equilibrium. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and ____ in human blood is one of the processes involving human health.
e: The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and oxygen in human blood is one of the processes involving human health. Oxygen: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: A chemical equilibrium is a ____ equilibrium; that is, reactants are continuously being changed to products and products are continuously being changed back to reactants.
e: A chemical equilibrium is a dynamic equilibrium; that is, reactants are continuously being changed to products and products are continuously being changed back to reactants. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: Many chemical reactions go to completion, but some reactions do not go to completion, and they can be ____.
e: Many chemical reactions go to completion, but some reactions do not go to completion, and they can be reversed. Reversed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the ____ reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants.
e: There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the reverse reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants. The reverse reaction turns products back into reactants.

q: These reactions that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions under the appropriate conditions are ____ reactions.
e: These reactions that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions under the appropriate conditions are reversible reactions. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: The symbol $\rightleftharpoons$ is used to represent the ____ reaction.
e: The symbol equilibrium is used to represent the reversible reaction. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Reversible reactions that happen in a closed system eventually reach ____.
e: Reversible reactions that happen in a closed system eventually reach equilibrium. At equilibrium both directions still run, at equal rates.

q: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in ____.
e: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in equilibrium. At equilibrium both directions still run, at equal rates.

q: If a reversible reaction is in a closed system, the system can reach a state called a ____ equilibrium.
e: If a reversible reaction is in a closed system, the system can reach a state called a dynamic equilibrium. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions do not stop; rather, they continue to occur at the ____ rate.
e: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions do not stop; rather, they continue to occur at the same rate. Equal forward and reverse rates keep concentrations the same at equilibrium.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the continuous occurrence of forward and reverse reactions at the same rate leads to ____ concentrations of the reactants and products.
e: In dynamic equilibrium, the continuous occurrence of forward and reverse reactions at the same rate leads to constant concentrations of the reactants and products. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: As the reaction proceeds towards equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants gradually ____, whereas the concentrations of products gradually increase.
e: As the reaction proceeds towards equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants gradually decrease, whereas the concentrations of products gradually increase. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain ____.
e: After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain constant. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: As depicted in the reaction rates figure, the rate of the forward reaction is ____ and the rate of the reverse reaction is low initially.
e: As depicted in the reaction rates figure, the rate of the forward reaction is high and the rate of the reverse reaction is low initially. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction ____ until both reactions occur at the same rate.
e: As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction increases until both reactions occur at the same rate. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: The equilibrium is reached when the two rates are ____.
e: The equilibrium is reached when the two rates are equal. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Based on the phase of the reactants and products, chemical equilibrium can be classified into homogeneous and ____ chemical equilibria.
e: Based on the phase of the reactants and products, chemical equilibrium can be classified into homogeneous and heterogeneous chemical equilibria. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: In homogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a ____ phase.
e: In homogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a single phase. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: An example of homogeneous chemical equilibrium is $N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons$ ____.
e: An example of homogeneous chemical equilibrium is N2(g) + O2(g) equilibrium 2NO(g). Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are present in ____ than one phase.
e: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are present in more than one phase. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: An example of heterogeneous chemical equilibrium is $Fe_2O_3(s) + 3CO(g) \rightleftharpoons$ ____.
e: An example of heterogeneous chemical equilibrium is Fe2O3(s) + 3CO(g) equilibrium 2Fe(s)+3CO2(g). Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: A ____ reaction is a reaction that can proceed in the forward as well as in the reverse directions under the appropriate conditions.
e: A reversible reaction is a reaction that can proceed in the forward as well as in the reverse directions under the appropriate conditions. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: A ____ system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor lost.
e: A closed system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor lost. Closed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: ____ equilibrium is a chemical equilibrium in which the reaction is still proceeding at equal rates of the forward and reverse reactions, and the concentrations of the reactants and products remain constant.
e: Dynamic equilibrium is a chemical equilibrium in which the reaction is still proceeding at equal rates of the forward and reverse reactions, and the concentrations of the reactants and products remain constant. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: ____ equilibrium is one in which the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a single phase.
e: Homogeneous equilibrium is one in which the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a single phase. Homogeneous means every species is in the same phase.

q: ____ equilibrium is one in which the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in more than one phase.
e: Heterogeneous equilibrium is one in which the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in more than one phase. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal, and thus the concentrations of reactants and products remain ____.
e: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal, and thus the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: Le Chatelier's principle is a qualitative guide to the effect of changes in concentration, temperature, and ____ on a system at equilibrium.
e: Le Chatelier's principle is a qualitative guide to the effect of changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure on a system at equilibrium. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: When one of these factors (stress) changes, the position of chemical equilibrium is effectively ____.
e: When one of these factors (stress) changes, the position of chemical equilibrium is effectively altered. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Le Chatelier's principle was discovered by French Chemist Henri Louis Le Chatelier in the year ____.
e: Le Chatelier's principle was discovered by French Chemist Henri Louis Le Chatelier in the year 1884. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: Le Chatelier's principle can be stated as: If a system is in equilibrium and when any of the factors affecting the chemical equilibrium is changed, the equilibrium shifts so as to ____ out the effect of the change.
e: Le Chatelier's principle can be stated as: If a system is in equilibrium and when any of the factors affecting the chemical equilibrium is changed, the equilibrium shifts so as to cancel out the effect of the change. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: Once equilibrium is established in a system, no further change is apparent as long as the ____ factors remain unchanged.
e: Once equilibrium is established in a system, no further change is apparent as long as the external factors remain unchanged. External: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure of the system are ____ factors that affect equilibrium.
e: The changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure of the system are external factors that affect equilibrium. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: A change in concentration, temperature, or pressure makes a difference in the amount of product formed in a reaction, but a ____ does not affect the equilibrium concentrations.
e: A change in concentration, temperature, or pressure makes a difference in the amount of product formed in a reaction, but a catalyst does not affect the equilibrium concentrations. The catalyst changes rate without being consumed in the overall equation.

q: A change in the concentration of one of the substances in an equilibrium system affects the equilibrium ____.
e: A change in the concentration of one of the substances in an equilibrium system affects the equilibrium positions. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Adding or removing a reactant or product from a reaction mixture at equilibrium will always ____ the equilibrium.
e: Adding or removing a reactant or product from a reaction mixture at equilibrium will always disturb the equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the system responds by removing the concentration of the reactant, and the reaction proceeds in the ____ direction.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the system responds by removing the concentration of the reactant, and the reaction proceeds in the forward direction. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the ____ to reestablish equilibrium.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the right to reestablish equilibrium. A shift to the right makes more products.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the ____ direction in favour of reactants.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction in favour of reactants. The reverse reaction turns products back into reactants.

q: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the ____ to reestablish equilibrium.
e: When the concentration of a reactant is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the left to reestablish equilibrium. A shift to the left makes more reactants.

q: When the concentration of a product is increased, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction in favour of reactants, and the equilibrium shifts to the ____.
e: When the concentration of a product is increased, the reaction proceeds in the reverse direction in favour of reactants, and the equilibrium shifts to the left. A shift to the left makes more reactants.

q: When the concentration of a product is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction in favour of products, and the equilibrium shifts to the ____.
e: When the concentration of a product is decreased, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction in favour of products, and the equilibrium shifts to the right. A shift to the right makes more products.

q: In the reaction $Fe^{3+}(aq) + SCN^-(aq) \rightleftharpoons FeSCN^{2+}(aq)$, increasing the concentration of $SCN^-$ favours the ____ reaction.
e: In the reaction Fe3+(aq) + SCN-(aq) equilibrium FeSCN2+(aq), increasing the concentration of SCN- favours the forward reaction. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: Changing the temperature can also affect the equilibrium ____.
e: Changing the temperature can also affect the equilibrium position. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The effect of temperature on chemical equilibrium depends upon the ____ changes ($\Delta H$) of the reaction.
e: The effect of temperature on chemical equilibrium depends upon the heat changes (deltaH) of the reaction. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: A temperature decrease favours an ____ reaction.
e: A temperature decrease favours an exothermic reaction. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: A temperature increase favours an ____ reaction.
e: A temperature increase favours an endothermic reaction. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: In the case of exothermic reactions, decreasing the temperature favours the exothermic reaction by releasing heat, and the equilibrium shifts towards the ____ reaction.
e: In the case of exothermic reactions, decreasing the temperature favours the exothermic reaction by releasing heat, and the equilibrium shifts towards the forward reaction. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: In the case of endothermic reactions, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction by absorbing heat, and the equilibrium shifts towards the ____ reaction.
e: In the case of endothermic reactions, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction by absorbing heat, and the equilibrium shifts towards the forward reaction. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: The decomposition of $N_2O_4$ (colourless) to $NO_2$ (reddish-brown) has a positive $\Delta H$, meaning the forward reaction is ____.
e: The decomposition of N2O4 (colourless) to NO2 (reddish-brown) has a positive deltaH, meaning the forward reaction is endothermic. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: For the decomposition of $N_2O_4$, when the temperature is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the ____, and more $N_2O_4$ is obtained.
e: For the decomposition of N2O4, when the temperature is decreased, the equilibrium shifts to the left, and more N2O4 is obtained. A shift to the left makes more reactants.

q: For the decomposition of $N_2O_4$, when the temperature is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the ____, and more $NO_2$ is obtained.
e: For the decomposition of N2O4, when the temperature is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the right, and more NO2 is obtained. A shift to the right makes more products.

q: In the reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$ with $\Delta H = (-)$, the forward reaction is an ____ reaction.
e: In the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) equilibrium 2NH3(g) with delta H = (-), the forward reaction is an exothermic reaction. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: For the ammonia synthesis reaction, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction, so the ____ reaction will be favoured.
e: For the ammonia synthesis reaction, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic reaction, so the reverse reaction will be favoured. The reverse reaction turns products back into reactants.

q: Pressure changes do not markedly affect the solid or ____ phases.
e: Pressure changes do not markedly affect the solid or liquid phases. Liquid is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Pressure has a significant effect on the ____ phase.
e: Pressure has a significant effect on the gas phase. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: The pressure of a gas mixture at a given temperature is determined by the number of gas molecules in a given ____.
e: The pressure of a gas mixture at a given temperature is determined by the number of gas molecules in a given volume. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: The effect of pressure depends on the total number of ____ of gases on each side of the chemical reactions.
e: The effect of pressure depends on the total number of moles of gases on each side of the chemical reactions. Moles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If the pressure is increased, the position of equilibrium will shift towards the side with ____ moles of gas.
e: If the pressure is increased, the position of equilibrium will shift towards the side with fewer moles of gas. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: If the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides of the reversible chemical equation, pressure has ____ effect.
e: If the number of moles of gas is the same on both sides of the reversible chemical equation, pressure has no effect. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: In the reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$, increasing the pressure by lowering the piston favours fewer moles of gas, so the equilibrium shifts to the ____.
e: In the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) equilibrium 2NH3(g), increasing the pressure by lowering the piston favours fewer moles of gas, so the equilibrium shifts to the right. A shift to the right makes more products.

q: In the reaction $2SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2SO_3(g)$, increasing pressure favours fewer moles of gases, so the ____ reaction will be favoured.
e: In the reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) equilibrium 2SO3(g), increasing pressure favours fewer moles of gases, so the forward reaction will be favoured. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: In the reaction $4CuO(s) \rightleftharpoons 2Cu_2O(s) + O_2(g)$, pressure affects only the ____ gas.
e: In the reaction 4CuO(s) equilibrium 2Cu2O(s) + O2(g), pressure affects only the oxygen gas. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: For the reaction $4CuO(s) \rightleftharpoons 2Cu_2O(s) + O_2(g)$, decreasing the pressure favours more moles of gas, so the ____ reaction will be favoured.
e: For the reaction 4CuO(s) equilibrium 2Cu2O(s) + O2(g), decreasing the pressure favours more moles of gas, so the forward reaction will be favoured. The forward reaction makes products from reactants.

q: In the reaction $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$, the number of moles of reactants is ____ to that of the product.
e: In the reaction H2(g) + I2(g) equilibrium 2HI(g), the number of moles of reactants is equal to that of the product. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: For the reaction $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$, increasing pressure causes ____ shift in equilibrium.
e: For the reaction H2(g) + I2(g) equilibrium 2HI(g), increasing pressure causes no shift in equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Industrial processes are usually designed to give the maximum possible ____ of products.
e: Industrial processes are usually designed to give the maximum possible yield of products. Yield is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The synthesis of ammonia (____ process) is a good example of an industrial process that uses Le Chatelier's principle.
e: The synthesis of ammonia (Haber process) is a good example of an industrial process that uses Le Chatelier's principle. Haber: le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: For ammonia production, since the reaction is exothermic, the forward reaction is favoured at ____ temperatures.
e: For ammonia production, since the reaction is exothermic, the forward reaction is favoured at low temperatures. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: For ammonia production, the pressure must be maintained at a ____ level to get the highest quantity of ammonia.
e: For ammonia production, the pressure must be maintained at a high level to get the highest quantity of ammonia. High is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The catalyst used in the Haber process is iron(III) oxide with a small amount of ____ oxide.
e: The catalyst used in the Haber process is iron(III) oxide with a small amount of aluminium oxide. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Methanol is produced from carbon monoxide and ____.
e: Methanol is produced from carbon monoxide and hydrogen. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: The forward reaction for methanol production ($CO(g) + 2H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)$) is ____.
e: The forward reaction for methanol production (CO(g) + 2H2(g) equilibrium CH3OH(g)) is exothermic. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: Methanol production is carried out at a temperature of ____ $^\circ$C using the catalyst $Cu-ZnO-Al_2O_3$.
e: Methanol production is carried out at a temperature of 250 degreesC using the catalyst Cu-ZnO-Al2O3. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the pressure will shift the equilibrium of methanol production to form ____ moles of methanol.
e: According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the pressure will shift the equilibrium of methanol production to form more moles of methanol. Le Chatelier's principle says a system at equilibrium shifts to oppose a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature.

q: In 1864, two Norwegian chemists proposed the law of ____ action as a general description of the equilibrium condition.
e: In 1864, two Norwegian chemists proposed the law of mass action as a general description of the equilibrium condition. Mass: equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The law of mass action is a quantitative law for predicting the amounts of reactants and products when a reaction reaches a state of ____ equilibrium.
e: The law of mass action is a quantitative law for predicting the amounts of reactants and products when a reaction reaches a state of dynamic equilibrium. Dynamic means the reactions have not stopped; they are balanced.

q: According to the law of mass action, for a reversible reaction at equilibrium and a constant temperature, the ratio between the concentration of reactants and products is ____.
e: According to the law of mass action, for a reversible reaction at equilibrium and a constant temperature, the ratio between the concentration of reactants and products is constant. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: The rate of the forward reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants raised to a power equal to their ____.
e: The rate of the forward reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactants raised to a power equal to their coefficients. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The rate of the reverse reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the products raised to a power equal to its ____.
e: The rate of the reverse reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the products raised to a power equal to its coefficients. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: At equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are ____.
e: At equilibrium, the rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations, with each concentration raised to the power corresponding to its coefficient, is called the equilibrium ____.
e: The ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations, with each concentration raised to the power corresponding to its coefficient, is called the equilibrium constant. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: The equilibrium constant, $K_{eq}$, is a characteristic numerical value only at a specified ____.
e: The equilibrium constant, Keq, is a characteristic numerical value only at a specified temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: The equilibrium constant provides how far a reaction has gone towards ____ before it reaches equilibrium.
e: The equilibrium constant provides how far a reaction has gone towards completion before it reaches equilibrium. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: Pure solids or liquids are excluded from the equilibrium expression because their concentrations remain ____ throughout the reaction.
e: Pure solids or liquids are excluded from the equilibrium expression because their concentrations remain constant throughout the reaction. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is large ($K_{eq} \gg 1$), the equilibrium lies to the ____ and there are more products than reactants.
e: If the Keq value is large (Keq1), the equilibrium lies to the right and there are more products than reactants. A shift to the right makes more products.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is small ($K_{eq} \ll 1$), the equilibrium lies to the ____ and there are more reactants than products.
e: If the Keq value is small (Keq1), the equilibrium lies to the left and there are more reactants than products. A shift to the left makes more reactants.

q: If the $K_{eq}$ value is equal to one ($K_{eq} = 1$), both reactants and products are ____ favoured at equilibrium.
e: If the Keq value is equal to one (Keq = 1), both reactants and products are equally favoured at equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: If molar concentrations are used, the equilibrium constant can be expressed as ____.
e: If molar concentrations are used, the equilibrium constant can be expressed as Kc. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: For equilibrium that involves gases, pressure can be used instead of concentration, and the equilibrium constant is written as ____.
e: For equilibrium that involves gases, pressure can be used instead of concentration, and the equilibrium constant is written as Kp. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: Both $K_c$ and $K_p$ can be applied for ____ reactions.
e: Both Kc and Kp can be applied for gaseous reactions. Kp is the equilibrium constant written with partial pressures of gases.

q: For a homogeneous equilibrium, e.g., $H_2(g) + I_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2HI(g)$, the equilibrium constant can be expressed as $K_{eq} = \frac{[HI]^2}{[H_2][I_2]}$. The concentration of $HI$ is raised to the power of ____.
e: For a homogeneous equilibrium,, H2(g) + I2(g) equilibrium 2HI(g), the equilibrium constant can be expressed as Keq = [HI]2[H2][I2]. The concentration of HI is raised to the power of 2. In a homogeneous equilibrium every species is in the same phase, often all aqueous or all gas.

q: In a liquid-vapour heterogeneous equilibrium state, e.g., $C_2H_5OH(l) \rightleftharpoons C_2H_5OH(g)$, the equilibrium constant expression becomes $K_{eq} = $ ____.
e: In a liquid-vapour heterogeneous equilibrium state,, C2H5OH(l) equilibrium C2H5OH(g), the equilibrium constant expression becomes Keq = [C2H5OH(g)]. In a heterogeneous equilibrium at least two phases are present, such as a solid with a gas.

q: Because ethanol is a pure liquid, its concentration is ____ at a given temperature.
e: Because ethanol is a pure liquid, its concentration is constant at a given temperature. An equilibrium constant is constant only at a fixed temperature.

q: The equilibrium for the sublimation of iodine crystals ($I_2(s) \rightleftharpoons I_2(g)$) is an example of the solid-vapour ____ equilibrium state.
e: The equilibrium for the sublimation of iodine crystals (I2(s) equilibrium I2(g)) is an example of the solid-vapour heterogeneous equilibrium state. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: For the sublimation of iodine crystals, the equilibrium constant expression becomes $K_{eq} = $ ____.
e: For the sublimation of iodine crystals, the equilibrium constant expression becomes Keq = [I2(g)]. The equilibrium constant is the ratio of product amounts to reactant amounts at equilibrium at a fixed temperature.

q: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant is determined by measuring the concentration of each substance involved in a chemical reaction at ____.
e: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant is determined by measuring the concentration of each substance involved in a chemical reaction at equilibrium. At equilibrium both directions still run, at equal rates.

q: The equilibrium constant is a ratio that expresses the relationship between the amounts of products and reactants present at equilibrium in a reversible chemical reaction at a given ____.
e: The equilibrium constant is a ratio that expresses the relationship between the amounts of products and reactants present at equilibrium in a reversible chemical reaction at a given temperature. Temperature is the one stress that can change the value of K.

q: Hydrogen and bromine reversibly react as $H_2(g) + Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons$ ____.
e: Hydrogen and bromine reversibly react as H2(g) + Br2(g) equilibrium 2HBr(g). Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Ammonia is prepared from nitrogen and hydrogen, and the heat evolved in the reaction is ____ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
e: Ammonia is prepared from nitrogen and hydrogen, and the heat evolved in the reaction is 29 kJ mol-1. 29 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the equilibrium $2Cl_2(g) + 2H_2O(g) \rightleftharpoons 4HCl(g) + O_2(g)$, the forward reaction is ____ because $\Delta H = (+)$.
e: In the equilibrium 2Cl2(g) + 2H2O(g) equilibrium 4HCl(g) + O2(g), the forward reaction is endothermic because delta H = (+). The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.
